purpose: Mafenide is a cream or solution applied directly to burn wounds to help prevent and treat infections. It is commonly used in hospital burn centers to protect serious burns from getting infected. Keeping burns free from infection is very important for healing.
how_it_works: Mafenide is an antibiotic that kills or stops the growth of bacteria on the surface of burns. It works by blocking a step that bacteria need to make an important building block called folic acid, which bacteria need to survive and grow. Without this, the bacteria cannot multiply and the infection is kept under control.
common_side_effects: You may feel a burning or stinging sensation when the cream or solution is first applied to the wound — this is common and usually goes away. Some people may develop a skin rash or itching in the treated area. Rarely, it can affect your breathing or cause your body to have trouble balancing certain chemicals in the blood.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or lung problems before using this medication, as mafenide can sometimes affect kidney function and the balance of acids in your blood. If you feel short of breath, breathe faster than normal, or feel very tired, let your medical team know right away. People who are allergic to sulfa drugs should inform their doctor, as a reaction is possible. Do not use this medication on your own without medical supervision — it is typically used in a hospital or wound care setting.
typical_dosing: A thin layer of mafenide cream is applied to the cleaned burn wound once or twice a day by a nurse or healthcare provider. For the solution form, it is used to keep dressings on the wound moist, usually changed every few hours. Your medical team will decide the exact schedule based on the size and severity of your burns.
